title: Exact descent of a continuous realization cocone through common finite stages
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite $E\subset\Omega$ put $B_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $E_T=B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$, and $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ valued in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal C_E(T)=D^b_c(T,E)$ for the raw rationalization of derived-complete integral constructible complexes, with its specified completed finite scalar transitions $S_{F/E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the common-stage pair category of these $\mathcal C_E(T)$, with Hom groups the directed colimits over common finite fields [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $A=E_T,R_T$, let $\mathcal D_T(A)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of bounded objects whose cohomology sheaves have a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which they are pro-etale locally finite free over $A$.

Suppose for every finite $E$ one is given the exact $E$-linear equivalence $J_{E,T}:\mathcal C_E(T)\simeq\mathcal D_T(E_T)$ induced by $E_T\otimes^L_{B_{E,T}}-$, together with the natural scalar comparisons $j_{F/E}:J_{F,T}S_{F/E}\simeq(F_T\otimes^L_{E_T}-)J_{E,T}$ induced by the specified quotient-completion comparison and balanced multiplication. Assume their identity and tower equations with the actual scalar transitions [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], including after extension to $R_T$.

The formulas $\rho_T(E,K)=R_T\otimes^L_{E_T}J_{E,T}K$ and, on an arrow represented by $u$ over $F$, scalar extension of $J_{F,T}(u)$ conjugated by these comparisons, define a functor independent of the chosen common field and of the representative arrow. Its maps on Hom groups are the canonical bijections
$$\varinjlim_{F\supset E,E'}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_F(T)}(S_{F/E}K,S_{F/E'}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_T)}(\rho_T(E,K),\rho_T(E',L)).$$
Every object of $\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ is isomorphic to some $\rho_T(E,K)$. The functor preserves shifts and distinguished triangles with their finite-stage normalization: a distinguished triangle represented over one finite field is sent to its derived scalar extension. Consequently $\rho_T:\mathcal C_T\simeq\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ is an exact equivalence with these specified object and arrow formulas.

source.place: BS Proposition 6.8.14; HRS Proposition 5.2 and Lemma 7.9; common-stage object, Hom and triangle descent, old steps 4--6; HRS: literature/hemo-richarz-scholbach-constructible-sheaves_arXiv-2305.18131.pdf; precise map normalization is the agent-written argument retained in report.md.

proof.text: The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its affine ring has only the ideals $0,k$. Finite type over a Noetherian scheme makes $T$ Noetherian. Its underlying space is Noetherian: by the definition of finite type, $T$ has a finite cover by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with $B_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, and each $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is a Noetherian space because the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is. An ascending chain of opens of $T$ stabilizes on each of the finitely many $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, hence on $T$. A subspace $Z$ of a Noetherian space is Noetherian: if $Z\cap U_1\subset Z\cap U_2\subset\cdots$ with $U_n$ open, put $V_n=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_n$; then $Z\cap V_n=Z\cap U_n$ and the chain $V_n$ stabilizes. So every locally closed stratum is topologically Noetherian. Also $T$ is qcqs because it is separated of finite type over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus the Noetherian and qcqs hypotheses of the coefficient comparison and descent results below hold, including on every stratum.

source.place: Proposition 5.2 and Lemma 7.9, hypotheses; verification for the present finite-type schemes

proof.text: Identify the coefficient rings before comparing categories. The pulled-back coefficient identities give $p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}\cong B_{E,T}$ and $p_T^*\underline E\cong B_{E,T}[1/\ell]$. In the DVR $\mathcal O_E$, write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e>0$; hence inverting $\ell$ or $\varpi_E$ has the same universal property. This identifies $p_T^*\underline E$ with the actual $E_T$, and the closure ring is exactly $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, with finite-extension-valued sections. Use the internal-module/section-module equivalence to pass from the module objects in the condensed descent theorem to ordinary ring-sheaf modules. It leaves the underlying sheaves and arrows unchanged. Its exact tensor comparison sends a local pure tensor to the same pure tensor and preserves K-flat complexes; consequently termwise localization identifies derived scalar extension with the ordinary ringed-site derived scalar extension used here. For change of rings, both balanced maps send $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes m$; their inverses have the same formula, so the scalar comparison and its multiplication transitivity maps agree. All sites are taken small in the coefficient universe as in the cited module equivalence.

source.place: Section 6.8, continuous coefficient rings; ordinary internal-to-section module identification and balancing argument

proof.text: Under step 2, the bounded constructible categories in the condensed two-colimit theorem are precisely $\mathcal D_T(E_T)$ and $\mathcal D_T(R_T)$. Indeed the finite-field local-triviality lemma converts local finite presentations into finite free modules on each Noetherian stratum; the algebraic-closure local-triviality lemma does the same for $R_T$, using exactly the finite-extension-valued coefficient ring. Conversely a finite free module has the finite presentation $A^0\to A^r\to A^r\to0$, including $r=0$. The module equivalence preserves cohomology because it is exact, so boundedness and both stratified conditions coincide. The condensed two-colimit theorem therefore applies to these full subcategories and the actual derived scalar-extension functors, with the balanced multiplication comparisons identified in step 2.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, Lemma 7.9; BS Definition 6.8.8; constructibility comparison via the cited local-triviality statements

proof.text: Put $G_E=R_T\otimes^L_{E_T}J_{E,T}$. The given $j_{F/E}$ followed by balanced multiplication gives $\gamma_{F/E,K}:G_F(S_{F/E}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_EK$. For $u:S_{F/E}K\to S_{F/E'}L$, put $X_F=G_F(u)$ and define its image as $\gamma_{F/E',L}\circ X_F\circ\gamma_{F/E,K}^{-1}$. For $F\subset H$, let $a_K=\gamma_{H/F,S_{F/E}K}$ and $a_L=\gamma_{H/F,S_{F/E'}L}$, identifying iterated transitions with direct ones by the specified composition maps. Naturality gives $a_L\circ X_H=X_F\circ a_K$. The assumed tower equation gives $\gamma_{H/E,K}=\gamma_{F/E,K}\circ a_K$ and $\gamma_{H/E',L}=\gamma_{F/E',L}\circ a_L$. Substituting $X_H=a_L^{-1}\circ X_F\circ a_K$ into the formula at $H$ cancels both $a$ factors, giving exactly the formula at $F$. Equivalent representatives agree at a common further field by the pair-category definition, so have equal images. For composable arrows, move both to one common field; the adjacent factors $\gamma_{F/E',L}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{F/E',L}$ cancel, leaving the formula for their composite by functoriality of $G_F$. The identity equation gives preservation of identities. Thus this is the asserted functor with the specified arrow formula.

source.place: Lemma 7.9, normalized cocone assembly; explicit ordinary-category argument using the assumed identity and tower equations

proof.text: At each common finite $F$, full faithfulness of the assumed $J_{F,T}$ and conjugation by $j_{F/E},j_{F/E'}$ identify the source Hom group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_T(F_T)}(F_T\otimes^L_{E_T}J_{E,T}K,F_T\otimes^L_{E'_T}J_{E',T}L)$. Naturality and the assumed tower equations identify the transition maps on these groups. Thus these bijections induce inverse bijections on the directed colimits, by applying them to representatives. The Hom-surjectivity and eventual-equality clauses of the condensed two-colimit theorem, applied after step 3, identify this latter colimit with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_T)}(G_EK,G_{E'}L)$. Its map sends a representative to its scalar extension conjugated by multiplication. Step 2 and the definition of $\gamma$ identify that map with the formula of step 4. Hence these are the claimed canonical Hom bijections, and $\rho_T$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, full faithfulness; Lemma 7.9, finite coefficient-field specialization

proof.text: For $M\in\mathcal D_T(R_T)$, step 3 and object descent supply a finite $E$ and $N\in\mathcal D_T(E_T)$ with $R_T\otimes^L_{E_T}N\cong M$. Essential surjectivity of the assumed $J_{E,T}$ gives $K\in\mathcal C_E(T)$ with $J_{E,T}K\cong N$. Applying derived scalar extension yields $\rho_T(E,K)\cong M$. Full faithfulness from step 5 and these object isomorphisms produce a quasi-inverse: choose such a preimage for each object, and lift each conjugated arrow through the unique inverse of its Hom bijection. Uniqueness gives the functor laws and the two inverse natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 5.2, essential surjectivity; Lemma 7.9; elementary quasi-inverse assembly

proof.text: Derived change of rings $R_T\otimes^L_{E_T}-$ is exact for the canonical shift comparison, and $J_{E,T}$ is exact by hypothesis; so $G_E$ is exact with the composite shift comparison $\tau_{E,K}:G_E(K[1])\cong G_E(K)[1]$, and it sends each finite-stage distinguished triangle to its derived scalar extension, with its connecting morphism. The comparisons $\gamma$ commute with these shift comparisons. On a K-flat integral representative $P$ of $K$, the quotient-completion comparison inside $j_{F/E}$ satisfies $\alpha_{1,P}\chi_{P[1]}=\chi_P[1]$, where $\alpha$ is the shift comparison of the cone model of the integral scalar extension, which rationalizes to the shift comparison $\sigma_{F/E}$ of $S_{F/E}$; balanced multiplication and derived change of rings are computed termwise on the K-flat complexes $P$ and $P[1]$, so they commute with the termwise shift identifications; rationalization does not change objects. Hence $\tau_{E,K}\circ\gamma_{F/E,K[1]}=\gamma_{F/E,K}[1]\circ\tau_{F,S_{F/E}K}\circ G_F(\sigma_{F/E,K})$, so $\tau$ is natural for the arrows of step 4, not only for arrows over one field. Shifts and distinguished triangles of the pair category are represented over one finite field. Applying step 4 to those representatives gives precisely these shifted objects and these scalar-extended triangles; isomorphic triangles have isomorphic images. Thus $\rho_T$ with $\tau$ preserves shifts and distinguished triangles with the stated finite-stage normalization. Finally its essential image is the full category $\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ by step 6; this full subcategory is triangulated: lift the endpoints and arrow of a cone by full faithfulness, take its finite-stage cone in the source, and use the just-proved exactness to identify its image with an ambient cone. This proves the asserted exact equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14, triangulated comparisons; ordinary K-flat scalar extension and finite-stage distinguished triangles
